Benchmark Index
The ICE 2027 Maturity US Treasury UCITS Index tracks the performance of US Treasury notes and bonds with
maturities between 1 January 2027 and 2 December 2027, inclusive. To be eligible for inclusion in the Benchmark
Index securities must have a fixed coupon schedule and an amount outstanding, excluding amounts held in the
Federal Reserve’s SOMA account, of at least $1 billion. Inflation-linked debt and strips are excluded from the
Benchmark Index; however, the amounts outstanding of eligible securities are not reduced by any coupon portions
that have been stripped. US Treasury bills are not eligible for inclusion in the Benchmark Index except during the
cash reinvestment period in the maturity year as described below. Securities issued or marketed primarily to retail
investors are not eligible for inclusion in the Benchmark Index.

Cash flows from bond payments that are received during the month are retained in the Benchmark Index until the
end of the month and then are removed as part of the rebalancing process. Cash does not earn any reinvestment
income while it is held in the Benchmark Index.

Starting with the 31 January 2027 rebalancing, interest and principal payments received during the month will not
be removed from the Benchmark Index, and will be reinvested in the US Treasury bonds, US Treasury notes or US
Treasury bills that mature as close to, but after, 2 December 2027.

Benchmark Index constituents are market capitalization weighted based on amounts outstanding reduced by
amounts held in the Federal Reserve’s SOMA account, times price, plus accrued interest. The Benchmark Index
rebalances on a monthly. Further details regarding the Benchmark Index (including its constituents) are available
on the index provider’s website at https://indices.ice.com/ and https://indices.ice.com/publications#.

Please note that iShares iBonds Dec 2027 Term $ Treasury UCITS ETF has a defined term and holders

Fund may not be suitable for new investment in its final year or in the period approaching its final year.

In order to achieve this investment objective, the investment policy of the Fund is to invest in a portfolio of fixed
income securities that, as far as possible and practicable, consists of the component securities of the ICE 2028
Maturity Italy UCITS Index, this Fund’s Benchmark Index. The Fund intends to use optimisation techniques in order
to achieve a similar return to the Benchmark Index and it is therefore not expected that the Fund will hold each
and every underlying constituent of the Benchmark Index at all times or hold them in the same proportion as their
weightings in the Benchmark Index. The Fund may hold some securities which are not underlying constituents of
the Benchmark Index where such securities provide similar performance (with matching risk profile) to certain
securities that make up the Benchmark Index. However, from time to time the Fund may hold all constituents of
the Benchmark Index. The Fund is a defined term fund and Shareholders in the Fund on 2 December 2028 will
have their Shares redeemed on 3 December 2028 when all the bonds invested in by the Fund to provide the return
of the Benchmark Index are expected to have matured, without further notice or Shareholder approval. The Fund
will also be delisted from all relevant stock exchanges on or around that date (subject to individual stock exchange
requirements).

The Base Currency of iShares iBonds Dec 2028 Term € Italy Govt Bond UCITS ETF is Euro (€).

Benchmark Index
The ICE 2028 Maturity Italy UCITS Index tracks the performance of euro-denominated bonds issued by the
government of Italy with maturities between 1 January 2028 and 2 December 2028, inclusive. To be eligible for
inclusion in the Benchmark Index securities must have a fixed coupon schedule and an amount outstanding of at
least €1 billion. Inflation-linked debt is excluded from the Benchmark Index. Italian Government bills are not
eligible for inclusion in the Benchmark Index except during the cash reinvestment period in the maturity year as
described below. Securities issued or marketed primarily to retail investors are not eligible for inclusion in the
Benchmark Index.

Cash flows from bond payments that are received during the month are retained in the Benchmark Index until the
end of the month and then are removed as part of the rebalancing process. Cash does not earn any reinvestment
income while it is held in the Benchmark Index.

Starting with the 31 January 2028 rebalancing, interest and principal payments received during the month will not
be removed from the Benchmark Index, and will be reinvested in the Italian Government bonds or Italian
Government bills that mature as close to, but after, 2 December 2028 and which have an amount outstanding of
at least €5 billion.

Benchmark Index constituents are market capitalization weighted based on amounts outstanding, times price, plus
accrued interest. The Benchmark Index rebalances on a monthly. Further details regarding the Benchmark Index
(including its constituents) are available on the index provider’s website at https://indices.ice.com/ and
https://indices.ice.com/publications#.

Please note that iShares iBonds Dec 2028 Term € Italy Govt Bond UCITS ETF has a defined term and
holders of Shares in the Fund on 2 December 2028 will have their Shares redeemed without further
notice on 3 December 2028. Bonds invested in by the Fund to provide the return of the Benchmark
Index will mature throughout the final year of its term and it is important for investors to take this into
consideration before making any investment in the Fund in the final year and in the period approaching
the final year. For example, investors seeking exposure to corporate bonds should be aware that the
Fund may not be suitable for new investment in its final year or in the period approaching its final year.

Investment Objective
The investment objective of the Fund is to seek to provide investors with a total return, taking into account both
capital and income returns, which reflects the return of the Bloomberg MSCI December 2029 Maturity USD
Corporate ESG Screened Index.

Investment Policy
In order to achieve this investment objective, the investment policy of the Fund is to invest in a portfolio of fixed
income securities that, as far as possible and practicable, consists of the component securities of the Bloomberg
MSCI December 2029 Maturity USD Corporate ESG Screened Index, this Fund’s Benchmark Index. The Fund
intends to use optimisation techniques in order to achieve a similar return to the Benchmark Index and it is
therefore not expected that the Fund will hold each and every underlying constituent of the Benchmark Index at
all times or hold them in the same proportion as their weightings in the Benchmark Index. The Fund may hold
some securities which are not underlying constituents of the Benchmark Index where such securities provide similar
performance (with matching risk profile) to certain securities that make up the Benchmark Index. However, from
time to time the Fund may hold all constituents of the Benchmark Index. The Fund is a defined term fund and
Shareholders in the Fund on 2 December 2029 will have their Shares redeemed on 3 December 2029 when all the
bonds invested in by the Fund to provide the return of the Benchmark Index are expected to have matured, without
further notice or Shareholder approval. The Fund will also be delisted from all relevant stock exchanges on or
around that date (subject to individual stock exchange requirements).

The Fund's investments will, at the time of purchase, comply with the credit rating requirements of the Fund's
Benchmark Index, which is investment grade. While it is intended that the Fund's investments will comprise
investment grade issues that make up the Benchmark Index, issues may be downgraded in certain circumstances
from time to time. In such an event, the Fund may continue to hold the affected non-investment grade issues until
such time as the non-investment grade issues cease to form part of the Fund’s Benchmark Index and it is possible
and practicable (in the Investment Manager’s view) to liquidate the position.

It is intended that the Fund’s direct investments will, at the time of purchase, comply with the environmental,
social and governance (“ESG”) requirements and/or ESG ratings of the Fund's Benchmark Index. The Fund may
continue to hold securities which no longer comply with the ESG requirements and/or ESG ratings of the Fund's
Benchmark Index until such time as the relevant securities cease to form part of the Benchmark Index and it is
possible and practicable (in the Investment Manager's view) to liquidate the position.

The Base Currency of iShares iBonds Dec 2029 Term $ Corp UCITS ETF is US Dollar (US$).

Benchmark Index
The Bloomberg MSCI December 2029 Maturity USD Corporate ESG Screened Index measures the performance of
investment grade, US Dollar denominated, taxable fixed-rate corporate bonds, as defined by the index provider
and excludes issuers based on the index provider's ESG and other exclusionary criteria.

To be eligible for inclusion in the Benchmark Index the bonds must (i) be USD denominated; (ii) mature on or
between 1 January 2029 and 2 December 2029; (iii) have a minimum outstanding amount of US$300 million; and
(iv) be rated investment grade (Baa3/BBB-/BBB- or higher) by one or more of Moody’s, S&P and Fitch, using the
middle rating of Moody’s, Standard & Poor’s and Fitch; when a rating from only two agencies is available, the lower
is used; when only one agency rates a bond, that rating is used.

The Benchmark Index applies screens which exclude issuers that are involved in the following business
lines/activities (or related activities): tobacco, nuclear weapons, civilian firearms, controversial weapons (including
landmine manufacturing, cluster munitions, depleted uranium weapons, chemical and biological weapons), thermal
coal mining, generation of thermal coal power, oil sands, conventional weapons and weapons
systems/components/support systems/services. The index provider defines what constitutes “involvement” in each
restricted activity. This may be based on percentage of revenue, a defined total revenue threshold, or any
connection to a restricted activity regardless of the amount of revenue received.

The Benchmark Index also excludes issuers pursuant to ESG principles which measure each issuer's involvement
in major ESG controversies and how well they adhere to international norms and principles. The Benchmark Index
excludes issuers with a “Red” MSCI ESG Controversies score (less than 1) pursuant to ESG principles which
measure each issuer's involvement in major ESG controversies. The Benchmark Index further excludes issuers
that are not in compliance with the United Nations Global Compact Principles (which are widely accepted corporate
sustainability principles that meet fundamental responsibilities in areas such as anti-corruption, human rights,
labour and environment).

The Benchmark Index is market capitalisation weighted, with a 3% cap on any one issuer, and a pro rata
distribution of any excess weight across the Benchmark Index. The Benchmark Index rebalances on the last
calendar day of each month until one year prior to maturity. During this final year, the bonds comprised within the
Benchmark Index will gradually mature through the year and the Benchmark Index will no longer be updated or
rebalanced, except to remove securities at the end of each month which have been downgraded below investment
grade or no longer meet the ESG criteria.

The principal amount received from matured/downgraded bonds is replaced in the Benchmark Index with
government debt securities (T-bonds and T-bills) issued by the US Treasury, allocated across a number of issues,
each with an amount outstanding greater than or equal to US$5 billion.

Treasury bills that mature as close to, but after, 2 December 2029.

amounts held in the Federal Reserve’s SOMA account, times price, plus accrued interest. The Benchmark Index

measure each issuer's involvement in major ESG controversies. The Benchmark Index further excludes issuers
that are not in
compliance with the United Nations Global Compact Principles (which are widely accepted corporate sustainability
principles that meet fundamental responsibilities in areas such as anti-corruption, human rights, labour and
environment).

The Benchmark Index is market capitalisation weighted, with a 3% cap on any one issuer, and a pro rata
distribution of any excess weight across the Benchmark Index. The Benchmark Index rebalances on the last
calendar day of each month until one year prior to maturity. During this final year, the bonds comprised within the
Benchmark Index will gradually mature through the year and the Benchmark Index will no longer be updated or
rebalanced, except to remove securities at the end of each month which have been downgraded below investment
grade or no longer meet the ESG criteria.

The principal amount received from matured/downgraded bonds is replaced in the Benchmark Index with
government debt securities issued by Germany and France, allocated across a number of issues, each with an
amount outstanding greater than or equal to €5 billion.

The Benchmark Index excludes sovereign issuers subject to UNSC Trade Sanctions. This screen is applied
exclusively to government debt securities as they replace corporate bonds maturing in the final year of the
Benchmark Index.

Further details regarding the Benchmark Index (including its constituents) are available on the index provider’s
website at https://www.bloomberg.com/professional/product/indices/bloomberg-fixed-income-indices/#/ucits.

Please note that iShares iBonds Dec 2030 Term € Corp UCITS ETF has a defined term and holders of
Shares in the Fund on 2 December 2030 will have their Shares redeemed without further notice on 3
December 2030. Bonds invested in by the Fund to provide the return of the Benchmark Index will
mature throughout the final year of its term and it is important for investors to take this into
consideration before making any investment in the Fund in the final year and in the period approaching
the final year. For example, investors seeking exposure to corporate bonds should be aware that the
Fund may not be suitable for new investment in its final year or in the period approaching its final year.

iShares iBonds Dec 2031 Term $ Corp UCITS ETF

Investment Objective
The investment objective of the Fund is to seek to provide investors with a total return, taking into account both
capital and income returns, which reflects the return of the Bloomberg MSCI December 2031 Maturity USD
Corporate ESG Screened Index.

Investment Policy
In order to achieve this investment objective, the investment policy of the Fund is to invest in a portfolio of fixed
income securities that, as far as possible and practicable, consists of the component securities of the Bloomberg
MSCI December 2031 Maturity USD Corporate ESG Screened Index, this Fund’s Benchmark Index. The Fund
intends to use optimisation techniques in order to achieve a similar return to the Benchmark Index and it is
therefore not expected that the Fund will hold each and every underlying constituent of the Benchmark Index at
all times or hold them in the same proportion as their weightings in the Benchmark Index. The Fund may hold
some securities which are not underlying constituents of the Benchmark Index where such securities provide similar
performance (with matching risk profile) to certain securities that make up the Benchmark Index. However, from
time to time the Fund may hold all constituents of the Benchmark Index. The Fund is a defined term fund and
Shareholders in the Fund on 2 December 2031 will have their Shares redeemed on 3 December 2031 when all the
bonds invested in by the Fund to provide the return of the Benchmark Index are expected to have matured, without
further notice or Shareholder approval. The Fund will also be delisted from all relevant stock exchanges on or
around that date (subject to individual stock exchange requirements).

The Fund's investments will, at the time of purchase, comply with the credit rating requirements of the Fund's
Benchmark Index, which is investment grade. While it is intended that the Fund's investments will comprise
investment grade issues that make up the Benchmark Index, issues may be downgraded in certain circumstances
from time to time. In such an event, the Fund may continue to hold the affected non-investment grade issues until
such time as the non-investment grade issues cease to form part of the Fund’s Benchmark Index and it is possible

It is intended that the Fund’s direct investments will, at the time of purchase, comply with the environmental,

continue to hold securities which no longer comply with the ESG requirements and/or ESG ratings of the Fund's
Benchmark Index until such time as the relevant securities cease to form part of the Benchmark Index and it is
possible and practicable (in the Investment Manager's view) to liquidate the position.

The Base Currency of iShares iBonds Dec 2031 Term $ Corp UCITS ETF is US Dollar (US$).

Benchmark Index
The Bloomberg MSCI December 2031 Maturity USD Corporate ESG Screened Index measures the performance of
investment grade, US Dollar denominated, taxable fixed-rate corporate bonds, as defined by the index provider
and excludes issuers based on the index provider's ESG and other exclusionary criteria.

To be eligible for inclusion in the Benchmark Index the bonds must (i) be USD denominated; (ii) mature on or
between 1 January 2031 and 2 December 2031; (iii) comply with the requirements of the Benchmark Index in
relation to the minimum outstanding amount for each bond issuance; and (iv) be rated investment grade
(Baa3/BBB-/BBB- or higher) by one or more of Moody’s, S&P and Fitch, using the middle rating of Moody’s,
Standard & Poor’s and Fitch; when a rating from only two agencies is available, the lower is used; when only one
agency rates a bond, that rating is used.

The Benchmark Index applies screens which exclude issuers that are involved in the following business
lines/activities (or related activities): tobacco, nuclear weapons, civilian firearms, controversial weapons (including
landmine manufacturing, cluster munitions, depleted uranium weapons, chemical and biological weapons), thermal
coal mining, generation of thermal coal power, oil sands, conventional weapons and weapons
systems/components/support systems/services. The index provider defines what constitutes “involvement” in each
restricted activity. This may be based on percentage of revenue, a defined total revenue threshold, or any
connection to a restricted activity regardless of the amount of revenue received.

The Benchmark Index also excludes issuers pursuant to ESG principles which measure each issuer's involvement
in major ESG controversies and how well they adhere to international norms and principles. The Benchmark Index
excludes issuers with a “Red” MSCI ESG Controversies score (less than 1) pursuant to ESG principles which
measure each issuer's involvement in major ESG controversies. The Benchmark Index further excludes issuers
that are not in
compliance with the United Nations Global Compact Principles (which are widely accepted corporate sustainability
principles that meet fundamental responsibilities in areas such as anti-corruption, human rights, labour and
environment).

The Benchmark Index is market capitalisation weighted, with a 3% cap on any one issuer, and a pro rata
distribution of any excess weight across the Benchmark Index. The Benchmark Index rebalances on the last
calendar day of each month until one year prior to maturity. During this final year, the bonds comprised within the
Benchmark Index will gradually mature through the year and the Benchmark Index will no longer be updated or
rebalanced, except to remove securities at the end of each month which have been downgraded below investment
grade or no longer meet the ESG criteria.

During this final year, the principal amount received from matured/downgraded bonds is replaced in the Benchmark
Index with government debt securities (T-bonds and T-bills) issued by the US Treasury, allocated across a number
of issues, each adhering to the minimum outstanding amount requirements of the Benchmark Index.

The Benchmark Index excludes sovereign issuers subject to UNSC Trade Sanctions. This screen is applied
exclusively to government debt securities as they replace corporate bonds maturing in the final year of the
Benchmark Index.

Further details regarding the Benchmark Index (including its constituents) are available on the index provider’s
website at https://www.bloomberg.com/professional/product/indices/bloomberg-fixed-income-indices/#/ucits.

The Bloomberg MSCI December 2033 Maturity USD Corporate ESG Screened Index measures the performance of
investment grade, US Dollar denominated, taxable fixed-rate corporate bonds, as defined by the index provider
and excludes issuers based on the index provider's ESG and other exclusionary criteria.

To be eligible for inclusion in the Benchmark Index the bonds must (i) be USD denominated; (ii) mature on or
between 1 January 2033 and 2 December 2033; (iii) comply with the requirements of the Benchmark Index in
relation to the minimum outstanding amount for each bond issuance; and (iv) be rated investment grade
(Baa3/BBB-/BBB- or higher) by one or more of Moody’s, S&P and Fitch, using the middle rating of Moody’s,
Standard & Poor’s and Fitch; when a rating from only two agencies is available, the lower is used; when only one
agency rates a bond, that rating is used.

The Benchmark Index applies screens which exclude issuers that are involved in the following business
lines/activities (or related activities): tobacco, nuclear weapons, civilian firearms, controversial weapons (including
landmine manufacturing, cluster munitions, depleted uranium weapons, chemical and biological weapons), thermal
coal mining, generation of thermal coal power, oil sands, conventional weapons and weapons
systems/components/support systems/services. The index provider defines what constitutes “involvement” in each
restricted activity. This may be based on percentage of revenue, a defined total revenue threshold, or any
connection to a restricted activity regardless of the amount of revenue received.

The Benchmark Index also excludes issuers pursuant to ESG principles which measure each issuer's involvement
in major ESG controversies and how well they adhere to international norms and principles. The Benchmark Index
excludes issuers with a “Red” MSCI ESG Controversies score (less than 1) pursuant to ESG principles which
measure each issuer's involvement in major ESG controversies. The Benchmark Index further excludes issuers
that are not in
compliance with the United Nations Global Compact Principles (which are widely accepted corporate sustainability
principles that meet fundamental responsibilities in areas such as anti-corruption, human rights, labour and
environment).

The Benchmark Index is market capitalisation weighted, with a 3% cap on any one issuer, and a pro rata
distribution of any excess weight across the Benchmark Index. The Benchmark Index rebalances on the last
calendar day of each month until one year prior to maturity. During this final year, the bonds comprised within the
Benchmark Index will gradually mature through the year and the Benchmark Index will no longer be updated or
rebalanced, except to remove securities at the end of each month which have been downgraded below investment
grade or no longer meet the ESG criteria.

During this final year, the principal amount received from matured/downgraded bonds is replaced in the Benchmark
Index with government debt securities (T-bonds and T-bills) issued by the US Treasury, allocated across a number
of issues, each adhering to the minimum outstanding amount requirements of the Benchmark Index.

The Benchmark Index excludes sovereign issuers subject to UNSC Trade Sanctions. This screen is applied
exclusively to government debt securities as they replace corporate bonds maturing in the final year of the
Benchmark Index.

Further details regarding the Benchmark Index (including its constituents) are available on the index provider’s
website at https://www.bloomberg.com/professional/product/indices/bloomberg-fixed-income-indices/#/ucits.

Please note that iShares iBonds Dec 2033 Term $ Corp UCITS ETF has a defined term and holders of
Shares in the Fund on 2 December 2033 will have their Shares redeemed without further notice on 3
December 2033. Bonds invested in by the Fund to provide the return of the Benchmark Index will
mature throughout the final year of its term and it is important for investors to take this into
consideration before making any investment in the Fund in the final year and in the period approaching
the final year. For example, investors seeking exposure to corporate bonds should be aware that the
Fund may not be suitable for new investment in its final year or in the period approaching its final year.

(with matching risk profile) to certain securities that make up the Benchmark Index. However, from time to time
the Fund may hold all constituents of the Benchmark Index. The Fund is a defined term fund and Shareholders in
the Fund on 2 December 2035 will have their Shares redeemed on 3 December 2035 when all the bonds invested
in by the Fund to provide the return of the Benchmark Index are expected to have matured, without further notice
or Shareholder approval. The Fund will also be delisted from all relevant stock exchanges on or around that date
(subject to individual stock exchange requirements).

The Fund's investments will, at the time of purchase, comply with the credit rating requirements of the Fund's
Benchmark Index, which is investment grade. While it is intended that the Fund's investments will comprise
investment grade corporate bonds that make up the Benchmark Index, the credit ratings of the bonds may be
downgraded in certain circumstances from time to time. In such an event, the Fund may continue to hold the
affected non-investment grade bonds until such time as the non-investment grade bonds cease to form part of the
Fund’s Benchmark Index and it is possible and practicable (in the Investment Manager’s view) to liquidate the
position.

It is intended that the Fund’s direct investments will, at the time of purchase, comply with the environmental,
social and governance (“ESG”) requirements of the Fund's Benchmark Index. The Fund may continue to hold
securities which no longer comply with the ESG requirements of the Fund's Benchmark Index until such time as
the relevant securities cease to form part of the Benchmark Index and it is possible and practicable (in the
Investment Manager's view) to liquidate the position.

The Base Currency of iShares iBonds Dec 2035 Term € Corp UCITS ETF is Euro (€).

Benchmark Index
The Bloomberg MSCI December 2035 Maturity EUR Corporate ESG Screened Index measures the performance of
investment grade, Euro-denominated, taxable fixed-rate corporate bonds, as defined by the index provider and
excludes issuers based on the index provider's ESG and other exclusionary criteria.

To be eligible for inclusion in the Benchmark Index the bonds must (i) be Euro-denominated; (ii) mature on or
between 1 January 2035 and 2 December 2035; (iii) comply with the requirements of the Benchmark Index in
relation to the minimum outstanding amount for each bond issuance; and (iv) be rated investment grade
(Baa3/BBB-/BBB- or higher) by one or more of Moody’s, S&P and Fitch, using the middle rating of Moody’s,
Standard & Poor’s and Fitch; when a rating from only two agencies is available, the lower is used; when only one
agency rates a bond, that rating is used.

The Benchmark Index applies screens which exclude issuers that are involved in the following business
lines/activities (or related activities): tobacco, nuclear weapons, civilian firearms, controversial weapons (including
landmine manufacturing, cluster munitions, depleted uranium weapons, chemical and biological weapons), thermal
coal mining, generation of thermal coal power, oil sands, conventional weapons and weapons
systems/components/support systems/services. The index provider defines what constitutes “involvement” in each
restricted activity. This may be based on percentage of revenue, a defined total revenue threshold, or any
connection to a restricted activity regardless of the amount of revenue received.

The Benchmark Index also excludes issuers pursuant to ESG principles which measure each issuer's involvement
in major ESG controversies and how well they adhere to international norms and principles. The Benchmark Index
excludes issuers with a “Red” MSCI ESG Controversies score (equal to zero) pursuant to ESG principles which
measure each issuer's involvement in major ESG controversies. The Benchmark Index further excludes issuers
that are not in
compliance with the United Nations Global Compact Principles (which are widely accepted corporate sustainability
principles that meet fundamental responsibilities in areas such as anti-corruption, human rights, labour and
environment).

The Benchmark Index is market capitalisation weighted, with a 3% cap on any one issuer, and a pro rata
distribution of any excess weight across the Benchmark Index. The Benchmark Index rebalances on the last
calendar day of each month until one year prior to maturity. During this final year, the bonds comprised within the
Benchmark Index will gradually mature through the year and the Benchmark Index will no longer be updated or
rebalanced, except to remove securities at the end of each month which have been downgraded below investment
grade or no longer meet the ESG criteria.

During this final year, the principal amount received from matured/downgraded bonds is replaced in the Benchmark
Index with government debt securities issued by Germany and France, allocated across a number of issues, each
adhering to the minimum outstanding amount requirements of the Benchmark Index.

The Benchmark Index excludes sovereign issuers subject to UNSC Trade Sanctions. This screen is applied
exclusively to government debt securities as they replace corporate bonds maturing in the final year of the
Benchmark Index.

Further details regarding the Benchmark Index (including its constituents) are available on the index provider’s
website at https://www.bloomberg.com/professional/product/indices/bloomberg-fixed-income-indices/#/ucits.

up the Benchmark Index. However, from time to time the Fund may hold all constituents of the Benchmark
Index. The Fund is a defined term fund and Shareholders in the Fund on 2 December 2037 will have their
Shares redeemed on 3 December 2037 when all the bonds invested in by the Fund to provide the return of
the Benchmark Index are expected to have matured, without further notice or Shareholder approval. The
Fund will also be delisted from all relevant stock exchanges on or around that date (subject to individual stock
exchange requirements).

The Fund's investments will, at the time of purchase, comply with the credit rating requirements of the Fund's
Benchmark Index, which is investment grade. While it is intended that the Fund's investments will comprise
investment grade corporate bonds that make up the Benchmark Index, the credit ratings of the bonds may
be downgraded in certain circumstances from time to time. In such an event, the Fund may continue to hold
the affected non-investment grade bonds until such time as the non-investment grade bonds cease to form
part of the Fund’s Benchmark Index and it is possible and practicable (in the Investment Manager’s view) to
liquidate the position.

It is intended that the Fund’s direct investments will, at the time of purchase, comply with the environmental,
social and governance (“ESG”) requirements of the Fund's Benchmark Index. The Fund may continue to hold
securities which no longer comply with the ESG requirements of the Fund's Benchmark Index until such time
as the relevant securities cease to form part of the Benchmark Index and it is possible and practicable (in the
Investment Manager's view) to liquidate the position.

SFDR

The Fund promotes environmental characteristics related to: (i) reduction of non-renewable natural resource
utilisation and pollution; and (ii) reduction of very severe environmental related controversies, in line with its
Benchmark Index. The Fund promotes social characteristics related to: (i) reduction of the availability of weapons;
(ii) better health and wellbeing; (iii) support for human rights, labour standards, the environment and anti-
corruption; and (iv) reduction of very severe social related controversies, in line with its Benchmark Index. Details
of the environmental and social characteristics promoted by the Fund are set out in Schedule VII.

The Fund seeks to achieve this by tracking its Benchmark Index which has a methodology that is aligned with
attaining the environmental and/or social characteristics promoted by the Fund through the exclusion of issuers
involved in activities that are considered to be inconsistent with such characteristics.

Schedule VII sets out further information on the pre-contractual disclosures, as required under the SFDR and the
Taxonomy Regulation for the Fund. The pre-contractual disclosures have been prepared based on information
available from the index provider and other third-party data providers shortly prior to the date of this Prospectus.

While the index provider of the Benchmark Index of the Fund provides a description of what the Benchmark Index
is designed to achieve, index providers do not generally provide any warranty or accept any liability in relation to
the quality, accuracy or completeness of data in respect of their benchmark indices, nor any guarantee that the
published indices will be in line with their described benchmark index methodologies. Errors in respect of the quality,
accuracy and completeness of the data may occur from time to time and may not be identified and corrected for a
period of time, in particular where the indices are less commonly used.

Benchmark Index

The Bloomberg MSCI December 2037 Maturity EUR Corporate ESG Screened Index measures the performance
of investment grade, Euro-denominated, taxable fixed-rate corporate bonds, as defined by the index provider
and excludes issuers based on the index provider's ESG and other exclusionary criteria.

To be eligible for inclusion in the Benchmark Index the bonds must (i) be Euro -denominated; (ii) mature on



                                                         79

                                                                                             NM0926U-5898621-79/664

=== pdf p.80 ===
or between 1 January 2037 and 2 December 2037; (iii) comply with the requirements of the Benchmark Index
in relation to the minimum outstanding amount for each bond issuance; and (iv) be rated investment grade
(Baa3/BBB-/BBB- or higher) by one or more of Moody’s, S&P and Fitch, using the middle rating of Moody’s,
Standard & Poor’s and Fitch; when a rating from only two agencies is available, the lower is used; when only
one agency rates a bond, that rating is used.

The Benchmark Index applies screens which exclude issuers that are involved in the following business
lines/activities (or related activities): tobacco, nuclear weapons, civilian firearms, controversial weapons
(including landmine manufacturing, cluster munitions, depleted uranium weapons, chemical and biological
weapons), thermal coal mining, generation of thermal coal power, oil sands, conventional weapons and
weapons systems/components/support systems/services. The index provider defines what constitutes
“involvement” in each restricted activity. This may be based on percentage of revenue, a defined total revenue
threshold, or any connection to a restricted activity regardless of the amount of revenue received.

The Benchmark Index also excludes issuers pursuant to ESG principles which measure each issuer's
involvement in major ESG controversies and how well they adhere to international norms and principles. The
Benchmark Index excludes issuers with a “Red” MSCI ESG Controversies score (equal to zero) pursuant to
ESG principles which measure each issuer's involvement in major ESG controversies. The Benchmark Index
further excludes issuers that are not in compliance with the United Nations Global Compact Principles (which
are widely accepted corporate sustainability principles that meet fundamental responsibilities in areas such
as anti-corruption, human rights, labour and environment).

The Benchmark Index is market capitalisation weighted, with a 3% cap on any one issuer, and a pro rata
distribution of any excess weight across the Benchmark Index. The Benchmark Index rebalances on the last
calendar day of each month until one year prior to maturity. During this final year, the bonds comprised
within the Benchmark Index will gradually mature through the year and the Benchmark Index will no longer
be updated or rebalanced, except to remove securities at the end of each month which have been downgraded
below investment grade or no longer meet the ESG criteria.

During this final year, the principal amount received from matured/downgraded bonds is replaced in the
Benchmark Index with government debt securities issued by Germany and France, allocated across a number
of issues, each adhering to the minimum outstanding amount requirements of the Benchmark Index.

The Benchmark Index excludes sovereign issuers subject to UNSC Trade Sanctions. This screen is applied
exclusively to government debt securities as they replace corporate bonds maturing in the final year of the
Benchmark Index.

Further details regarding the Benchmark Index (including its constituents) are available on the index
provider’s website at https://www.bloomberg.com/professional/products/indices/fixed-income/#/ucits.

Please note that the iShares iBonds Dec 2037 Term € Corp UCITS ETF has a defined term and
holders of Shares in the Fund on 2 December 2037 will have their Shares redeemed without further
notice on 3 December 2037. Bonds invested in by the Fund to provide the return of the Benchmark
Index will mature throughout the final year of its term and it is important for investors to take this
into consideration before making any investment in the Fund in the final year and in the period
approaching the final year. For example, investors seeking exposure to corporate bonds should be
aware that the Fund may not be suitable for new investment in its final year or in the period
approaching its final year.

Benchmark Index
The J.P. Morgan CEMBI Broad Diversified Core Index provides a benchmark for fixed-rate and floating-rate
corporate debt securities that represent the total return performance of the US Dollar denominated emerging
market corporate debt universe. To be eligible for inclusion in the Benchmark Index, issuers must meet one of the
following criteria: (1) the issuers are headquartered in an emerging market country, or (2) 100% of the issuers’
operating assets are located within emerging markets economies, or (3) the issuers’ assets are 100% guaranteed
by an entity located within an emerging market economy. Only those instruments with at least five years until
maturity and with a current amount outstanding of US$500 million or more are considered for inclusion in the
Benchmark Index. Only US Dollar denominated bonds are included. Securities which have the amount of coupon
or redemption payment linked to a currency exchange rate are not eligible for inclusion. The Benchmark Index
currently includes bonds issued by corporations based in emerging market countries in Latin America, Eastern
Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia (excluding Japan).

There are currently no minimum credit rating requirements or credit rating restrictions on either the corporate
bonds or the country of issuance. Corporate issues in default will generally be removed from the Benchmark Index
at the following index rebalance by the index provider. Bonds are considered to be in default where the issuer fails
to pay a scheduled coupon and/or principal payment. A corporate which has filed bankruptcy or insolvency papers
(or the local market equivalent) with the relevant authority is considered to be in default. If a default occurs, upon
the removal of the bond(s) of the corporate issuers in default from the Benchmark Index, the Fund will seek to
dispose of the relevant bond(s) during its month-end rebalance. The Fund may continue to hold such bonds until
such time as the Fund’s position in such bonds can be liquidated. The Benchmark Index rebalances on a monthly
basis. Further details regarding the Benchmark Index (including its constituents) are available on the index
provider’s website at https://www.jpmorgan.com/pages/jpmorgan/investbk/solutions/research/.

iShares MSCI EMU Climate Transition Aware UCITS ETF

Investment Objective
The investment objective of the Fund is to seek to provide investors with a total return, taking into account
both capital and income returns, which reflects the return of the MSCI EMU Transition Aware Select Index.

Investment Policy
In order to achieve this investment objective, the investment policy of the Fund is to invest in a portfolio of equity
securities that as far as possible and practicable consists of the component securities of the MSCI EMU Transition
Aware Select Index, the Fund’s Benchmark Index. The Fund intends to replicate the constituents of the Benchmark
Index by holding all of the securities comprising the Benchmark Index in a similar proportion to their weightings
in the Benchmark Index. In order to replicate its Benchmark Index, this Fund may invest up to 20% of
its Net Asset Value in shares issued by the same body. This limit may be raised to 35% for a single
issuer when exceptional market conditions apply (as set out in section 4 of Schedule III).

It is intended that the Fund’s direct investments will, at the time of purchase, comply with the environmental,
social and governance (“ESG”) requirements and/or ESG ratings of the Fund's Benchmark Index. The Fund may
continue to hold securities which no longer comply with the ESG requirements and/or ESG ratings of the Fund's
Benchmark Index until such time as the relevant securities cease to form part of the Benchmark Index and it is
possible and practicable (in the Investment Manager's view) to liquidate the position.

For the purposes of complying with AMF ESG Rules, the Fund will adopt a best-in-class approach to sustainable
investing. The best-in-class approach means that by investing in a portfolio of securities that as far as possible and
practicable consists of the component securities of the Benchmark Index, it is expected that the Fund will invest in
the best issuers regarding their involvement in the transition to a low-carbon economy (based on the ESG and
inclusion criteria of the Benchmark Index). More than 90% of the net assets of the Fund, excluding Cash Holdings
and daily dealing money market collective investment schemes, are rated or analysed in accordance with the ESG
or inclusion criteria of the Benchmark Index. For FDI, any such analyses will apply only to the underlying securities.
As a result of the application of the ESG and inclusion criteria of the Benchmark Index, the Fund applies the
selectivity approach for the purposes of the AMF ESG Rules which means that the portfolio of the Fund is reduced
by at least 20% compared to the Parent Index (as defined below), calculated either (i) by number of issuers or (ii)
by the relative weighting of the worst performers in the Benchmark Index.

The Base Currency of iShares MSCI EMU Climate Transition Aware UCITS ETF is Euro (€).

Benchmark Index
The MSCI EMU Transition Aware Select Index measures the performance of a sub-set of equity securities within
the MSCI EMU Index (the “Parent Index”) which excludes issuers from the Parent Index based on the index
provider’s ESG exclusionary criteria. The remaining constituents of the Parent Index are then included in the
Benchmark Index in accordance with the index methodology on the basis of their involvement in the transition to
a low-carbon economy.

The Parent Index measures the performance of large and mid capitalisation stocks across developed markets
countries in the European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) which comply with MSCI's size, liquidity, and free-
float criteria. The list of eligible countries may be subject to change over time.

The Benchmark Index excludes issuers that are involved in the following business lines/activities (or related
activities): controversial weapons, tobacco, thermal coal and unconventional oil and gas. The index provider defines
what constitutes “involvement” in each restricted activity, this may be based on percentage of revenue, a defined
total revenue threshold, or any connection to a restricted activity regardless of the amount of revenue received.
Issuers that are classified as violating United Nations Global Compact principles (which are widely accepted
corporate sustainability principles that meet fundamental responsibilities in areas such as anti-corruption, human
rights, labour and environment) are also excluded.

The Benchmark Index also excludes companies from the Energy, Materials, Industrials and Utilities Global Industry
Classification Standard ("GICS") sectors if they meet any of the following criteria: i) have greenhouse gas
emissions intensity above a threshold as defined by the index provider, ii) do not yet have published emission
reduction targets, iii) do not report their greenhouse gas emissions to Carbon Disclosure Project, a not-for-profit
charity that runs the global disclosure system for companies to manage their environmental impacts.

The Benchmark Index also excludes companies which are identified by the index provider as being involved in


                                                        83

                                                                                            NM0926U-5898621-83/664

=== pdf p.84 ===
controversies that have a negative impact on their operations and/or products and services based on an MSCI
controversy score (“MSCI Controversy Score”). The minimum MSCI Controversy Score set by the index provider
to determine eligibility for inclusion in the Benchmark Index can be found at the index provider’s website at
https://www.msci.com/indexes/ishares.

Issuers that have not been assessed or rated by the index provider for an MSCI Controversy Score are excluded
from the Benchmark Index.

The remaining companies from the Parent Index are selected for inclusion in the Benchmark Index if they meet
any of the following criteria:
    -    Companies with a commitment to one or more active carbon emissions reduction target(s) approved by
         the Science Based Targets initiative (“SBTi”) are selected. The SBTi seeks to provide a clearly defined
         pathway for companies and financial institutions to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, helping
         prevent the worst impacts of climate change and future-proof business growth.
    -    Companies which generate green revenue that meet the threshold set by the index provider are selected.
         Green revenue is defined as the cumulative percentage of revenue a company derives from activities (or
         related activities) linked to a set of environmental impact themes including but not limited to alternative
         energy, energy efficiency and green building, as defined by the index provider.
    -    Companies from each GICS sector which also have published emissions reduction targets are ranked
         based on their GHG intensity. Starting from the lowest emissions intensity, companies are selected until
         the target sector coverage by cumulative free float-adjusted market capitalisation is reached, as
         determined by the index provider.

The Benchmark Index incorporates an iterative exclusion process in accordance with which the weight of the
selected securities may not be greater than 75% of the Parent Index.

Constraints to limit deviation from the constituent, country and sector weights of the Parent Index are applied in
accordance with the Benchmark Index methodology.

The Benchmark Index also seeks to allocate a proportion of the Benchmark Index to companies that either: (1)
derive a minimum percentage of their revenue from products or services with positive impacts on the environment
and/or society, or (2) have one or more active carbon emissions reduction target(s) approved by the Science Based
Targets initiative (SBTi).

The Benchmark Index is market capitalisation weighted and rebalances on a semi-annual basis. On a quarterly
basis, current constituents of the Benchmark Index are screened based on the index provider’s exclusion criteria.
Companies which have been identified as having a ‘red’ MSCI controversy flag, or which have been classified as
violating United Nations Global Compact principles, may also be removed from the Benchmark Index in between
index rebalances in accordance with the index methodology.

Further details regarding the Benchmark Index (including its constituents) are available on the index provider’s
website at https://www.msci.com/indexes/ishares and https://www.msci.com/constituents.

The Benchmark Index also excludes companies from the Energy, Materials, Industrials and Utilities Global Industry
Classification Standard ("GICS") sectors if they meet any of the following criteria: i) have greenhouse gas
emissions intensity above a threshold as defined by the index provider, ii) do not yet have published emission
reduction targets, iii) do not report their greenhouse gas emissions to Carbon Disclosure Project, a not-for-profit
charity that runs the global disclosure system for companies to manage their environmental impacts.

The Benchmark Index also excludes companies which are identified by the index provider as being involved in
controversies that have a negative impact on their operations and/or products and services based on an MSCI
controversy score (“MSCI Controversy Score”). The minimum MSCI Controversy Score set by the index provider
to determine eligibility for inclusion in the Benchmark Index can be found at the index provider’s website at
https://www.msci.com/indexes/ishares.

Issuers that have not been assessed or rated by the index provider for an MSCI Controversy Score are excluded
from the Benchmark Index.

The remaining companies from the Parent Index are selected for inclusion in the Benchmark Index if they meet
any of the following criteria:
    -    Companies with a commitment to one or more active carbon emissions reduction target(s) approved by
         the Science Based Targets initiative (“SBTi”) are selected. The SBTi seeks to provide a clearly defined
         pathway for companies and financial institutions to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, helping
         prevent the worst impacts of climate change and future-proof business growth.
    -    Companies which generate green revenue that meet the threshold set by the index provider are selected.
         Green revenue is defined as the cumulative percentage of revenue a company derives from activities (or
         related activities) linked to a set of environmental impact themes including but not limited to alternative
         energy, energy efficiency and green building, as defined by the index provider.
    -    Companies from each GICS sector which also have published emissions reduction targets are ranked
         based on their GHG intensity. Starting from the lowest emissions intensity, companies are selected until
         the target sector coverage by cumulative free float-adjusted market capitalisation is reached, as
         determined by the index provider.

The Benchmark Index incorporates an iterative exclusion process in accordance with which the weight of the
selected securities may not be greater than 75% of the Parent Index.

Constraints to limit deviation from the constituent, country and sector weights of the Parent Index are applied in
accordance with the Benchmark Index methodology.

The Benchmark Index also seeks to allocate a proportion of the Benchmark Index to companies that either: (1)
derive a minimum percentage of their revenue from products or services with positive impacts on the environment
and/or society, or (2) have one or more active carbon emissions reduction target(s) approved by the Science Based
Targets initiative (SBTi).

The Benchmark Index is market capitalisation weighted and rebalances on a semi-annual basis. On a quarterly
basis, current constituents of the Benchmark Index are screened based on the index provider’s exclusion criteria.
Companies which have been identified as having a ‘red’ MSCI controversy flag, or which have been classified as
violating United Nations Global Compact principles, may also be removed from the Benchmark Index in between
index rebalances in accordance with the index methodology.

Further details regarding the Benchmark Index (including its constituents) are available on the index provider’s
website at https://www.msci.com/indexes/ishares and https://www.msci.com/constituents.

iShares MSCI Global Telecommunication Services UCITS ETF

Investment Objective
The investment objective of the Fund is to seek to provide investors with a total return, taking into account both
capital and income returns, which reflects the return of the MSCI ACWI Select Telecommunication Services
Screened 35/20 Capped Index.

Investment Policy
In order to achieve this investment objective, the investment policy of the Fund is to invest in a portfolio of equity
securities that as far as possible and practicable consists of the component securities of the MSCI ACWI Select
Telecommunication Services Screened 35/20 Capped Index, this Fund’s Benchmark Index. The Fund intends to
replicate the constituents of the Benchmark Index by holding all of the securities comprising the Benchmark Index
in a similar proportion to their weightings in the Benchmark Index. In order to replicate its Benchmark Index,
this Fund may invest up to 20% of its Net Asset Value in shares issued by the same body. This limit
may be raised to 35% for a single issuer when exceptional market conditions apply (as set out in
section 4 of Schedule III).

The Base Currency of iShares MSCI Global Telecommunication Services UCITS ETF is US Dollar (US$).

Benchmark Index
The MSCI ACWI Select Telecommunication Services Screened 35/20 Capped Index aims to reflect the performance
of a sub-set of equity securities in the MSCI ACWI Telecommunication Services Index (the “Parent Index”)
excluding companies based on the index provider's exclusionary criteria and capping issuer exposure in accordance
with the index methodology.

The Parent Index is a free float-adjusted market capitalisation weighted index that comprises companies
included in the MSCI ACWI Index that are classified under the Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS)
Telecommunication Services industry group. The MSCI ACWI Index measures the performance of large and mid
capitalisation stocks across developed and emerging market countries which comply with MSCI’s size, liquidity and
free-float criteria.

The GICS telecommunication services industry group includes companies whose primary business involves the
provision of fixed-line, cellular and/or wireless telecommunication services; providers of communications and/or
high-density data transmission; producers of interactive gaming products and companies engaging in content and
information creation or distribution.

The Benchmark Index excludes companies that are classified as violating the United Nations Global Compact
principles (which are widely accepted corporate sustainability principles that meet fundamental responsibilities in
areas such as anti-corruption, human rights, labour and environmental).

To be eligible for inclusion in the Benchmark Index, companies must be domiciled in an eligible developed or
emerging market country as determined by the index provider.

The Benchmark Index also excludes companies which are identified by the index provider as being involved in
controversies that have a negative ESG impact on their operations and/or products and services based on an MSCI
ESG controversy score (“MSCI ESG Controversy Score”). The minimum MSCI ESG Controversy Score set by the
index provider to determine eligibility for inclusion in the Benchmark Index can be found at the index provider’s
website at https://www.msci.com/indexes/ishares.

The Benchmark Index rebalances on a quarterly basis. The Benchmark Index also caps the weight of the largest
companies at each rebalance to help ensure index diversification. The weight of the largest group entity in
the Benchmark Index is capped at 35% and the weights of the remaining group entities are cap ped at
20%.Additionally, the exclusion criteria are applied on a monthly basis.

The Fund may trade China A Shares via Stock Connect. Further details regarding the Benchmark Index (including
its constituents) are available on the index provider’s website at https://www.msci.com/indexes/ishares and
https://www.msci.com/constituents.

iShares MSCI Japan EUR Hedged UCITS ETF (Acc)

Investment Objective
The investment objective of the Fund is to provide investors with a total return, taking into account both capital
and income returns, which reflects the return of the MSCI Japan 100% Hedged to EUR Index Net.

Investment Policy
In order to achieve this investment objective, the investment policy of the Fund is to invest in a portfolio of equity
securities that as far as possible and practicable consist of the component securities of the MSCI Japan TR Index
and foreign exchange forward contracts that, as far as possible and practicable, track the hedging methodology of
the MSCI Japan 100% Hedged to EUR Index Net, this Fund’s Benchmark Index. Currency hedging is carried out
under a single hedging programme for the life of the Fund which is implemented using rolling one-month forward
contracts. The Fund intends to use optimisation techniques in order to achieve a similar return to the Benchmark
Index and it is therefore not expected that the Fund will hold each and every underlying constituent of the
Benchmark Index at all times or hold them in the same proportion as their weightings in the Benchmark Index.
The Fund may hold some securities which are not underlying constituents of the Benchmark Index where such
securities provide similar performance (with matching risk profile) to certain securities that make up the Benchmark
Index. However, from time to time the Fund may hold all constituents of the Benchmark Index.

The Base Currency of iShares MSCI Japan EUR Hedged UCITS ETF (Acc) is Euro (€).

Benchmark Index
The MSCI Japan 100% Hedged to EUR Index Net measures the performance of the MSCI Japan TR Index with
currency exposures hedged to Euro using one-month currency forwards according to the MSCI methodology. The
Benchmark Index contains both equity securities and foreign currency hedging components. The MSCI Japan TR
Index is designed to measure the performance of large and mid capitalisation stocks of the Japan equity market
which comply with MSCI's size, liquidity, and free-float criteria. The Benchmark Index incorporates a monthly
hedge, using a one month forward FX contract to reduce currency exposure. The foreign currency hedging
component      comprises     rolling  one-month     forward    contracts    that   are    reset   at   the   end
of each month and hedge each foreign currency in the Benchmark Index back to the Fund’s Base Currency (EUR).
No adjustment is made to the hedge during the month to account for price movements of constituent securities of
the Benchmark Index, corporate events affecting such securities, additions, deletions or any other changes to the
Benchmark Index. The Benchmark Index is market capitalisation weighted and rebalances on a semi-annual basis.
The Benchmark Index also undergoes quarterly reviews. These quarterly reviews may involve limited rebalancing,
consisting of the addition and/or removal of constituents from the Benchmark Index but not amounting to a full
reconstitution of the Benchmark Index. Further details regarding the Benchmark Index (including its constituents)
are   available     on   the    index  provider’s   website   at    https://www.msci.com/indexes/ishares     and
https://www.msci.com/constituents.

The Base Currency of iShares MSCI World Climate Transition Aware UCITS ETF is US Dollar (US$).

Benchmark Index
The MSCI World Transition Aware Select Index measures the performance of a sub-set of equity securities within
the MSCI World Index (the “Parent Index”) which excludes issuers from the Parent Index based on the index
provider’s ESG exclusionary criteria. The remaining constituents of the Parent Index are then included in the
Benchmark Index in accordance with the index methodology on the basis of their involvement in the transition to
a low-carbon economy.

The Parent Index measures the performance of large and mid capitalisation stocks across developed market
countries which comply with MSCI's size, liquidity and free-float criteria.

The Benchmark Index excludes issuers that are involved in the following business lines/activities (or related
activities): controversial weapons, tobacco, thermal coal and unconventional oil and gas. The index provider defines
what constitutes “involvement” in each restricted activity, this may be based on percentage of revenue, a defined
total revenue threshold, or any connection to a restricted activity regardless of the amount of revenue received.
Issuers that are classified as violating United Nations Global Compact principles (which are widely accepted
corporate sustainability principles that meet fundamental responsibilities in areas such as anti-corruption, human
rights, labour and environment) are also excluded.

The Benchmark Index also excludes companies from the Energy, Materials, Industrials and Utilities Global Industry
Classification Standard ("GICS") sectors if they meet any of the following criteria: i) have greenhouse gas
emissions intensity above a threshold as defined by the index provider, ii) do not yet have published emission
reduction targets, iii) do not report their greenhouse gas emissions to Carbon Disclosure Project, a not-for-profit
charity that runs the global disclosure system for companies to manage their environmental impacts.

The Benchmark Index also excludes companies which are identified by the index provider as being involved in
controversies that have a negative impact on their operations and/or products and services based on an MSCI
controversy score (“MSCI Controversy Score”). The minimum MSCI Controversy Score set by the index provider
to determine eligibility for inclusion in the Benchmark Index can be found at the index provider’s website at
https://www.msci.com/indexes/ishares.

Issuers that have not been assessed or rated by the index provider for an MSCI Controversy Score are excluded
from the Benchmark Index.

The remaining companies from the Parent Index are selected for inclusion in the Benchmark Index if they meet
any of the following criteria:


                                                        91

                                                                                            NM0926U-5898621-91/664

=== pdf p.92 ===
    -    Companies with a commitment to one or more active carbon emissions reduction target(s) approved by
         the Science Based Targets initiative (“SBTi”) are selected. The SBTi seeks to provide a clearly defined
         pathway for companies and financial institutions to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, helping
         prevent the worst impacts of climate change and future-proof business growth.
    -    Companies which generate green revenue that meet the threshold set by the index provider are selected.
         Green revenue is defined as the cumulative percentage of revenue a company derives from activities (or
         related activities) linked to a set of environmental impact themes including but not limited to alternative
         energy, energy efficiency and green building, as defined by the index provider.
    -    Companies from each GICS sector which also have published emissions reduction targets are ranked
         based on their GHG intensity. Starting from the lowest emissions intensity, companies are selected until
         the target sector coverage by cumulative free float-adjusted market capitalisation is reached, as
         determined by the index provider.

The Benchmark Index incorporates an iterative exclusion process in accordance with which the weight of the
selected securities may not be greater than 75% of the Parent Index.

Constraints to limit deviation from the constituent, country and sector weights of the Parent Index are applied in
accordance with the Benchmark Index methodology.

The Benchmark Index also seeks to allocate a proportion of the Benchmark Index to companies that either: (1)
derive a minimum percentage of their revenue from products or services with positive impacts on the environment
and/or society, or (2) have one or more active carbon emissions reduction target(s) approved by the Science Based
Targets initiative (SBTi).

The Benchmark Index is market capitalisation weighted and rebalances on a semi-annual basis. On a quarterly
basis, current constituents of the Benchmark Index are screened based on the index provider’s exclusion criteria.
Companies which have been identified as having a ‘red’ MSCI controversy flag, or which have been classified as
violating United Nations Global Compact principles, may also be removed from the Benchmark Index in between
index rebalances in accordance with the index methodology.

Further details regarding the Benchmark Index (including its constituents) are available on the index provider’s
website at https://www.msci.com/indexes/ishares and https://www.msci.com/constituents.

iShares MSCI World Communication Services Sector Advanced UCITS ETF

Investment Objective
The investment objective of the Fund is to seek to provide investors with a total return, taking into account both
capital and income returns, which reflects the return of the MSCI World Communication Services Advanced Select
20 35 Capped Index.

Investment Policy
In order to achieve this investment objective, the investment policy of the Fund is to invest in a portfolio of equity
securities that, as far as possible and practicable, consists of the component securities of the MSCI World
Communication Services Advanced Select 20 35 Capped Index, this Fund’s Benchmark Index. The Fund intends to
replicate the constituents of the Benchmark Index by holding all the securities comprising the Benchmark Index in
a similar proportion to their weightings in the Benchmark Index. In order to replicate its Benchmark Index,
this Fund may invest up to 20% of its Net Asset Value in shares issued by the same body. This limit
may be raised to 35% for a single issuer when exceptional market conditions apply (as set out in
section 4 of Schedule III).

For the purposes of complying with AMF ESG Rules, the Fund will adopt a binding and significant ESG optimisation
approach to sustainable investing. As part of this approach, the Fund will aim to invest in a portfolio of securities
that, as far as possible and practicable, consists of the component securities of the Benchmark Index, optimises
exposure to issuers in order to achieve a higher ESG rating and reduces exposure to carbon emissions compared
to the Parent Index while meeting other constraints of the ESG optimisation. More than 90% of the net assets of
the Fund, excluding Cash Holdings and daily dealing money market collective investment schemes, are rated or
analysed in accordance with the ESG criteria of the Benchmark Index. For FDI, any such analyses will apply only
to the underlying securities. By adopting the ESG methodology of the Benchmark Index, the Fund applies the
extra-financial indicator upgrade approach for the purposes of the AMF ESG Rules, which means that the weighted
average environmental indicator of the Fund (being the relevant extra-financial indicator of the Fund) will be at
least 20% better than the weighted average environmental indicator of the Parent Index (as defined below) based
on a reduction of carbon emission intensity.

The Base Currency of iShares MSCI World Communication Services Sector Advanced UCITS ETF is US Dollar
(US$).

Benchmark Index
The MSCI World Communication Services Advanced Select 20 35 Capped Index aims to reflect the
performance of a sub-set of equity securities in the MSCI World Communication Services Index (the " Parent
Index") which excludes issuers from the Parent Index based on the index provider's ESG and climate change -
related exclusionary criteria. The remaining constituents of the Parent Index are then weighted by the index
provider, for inclusion in the Benchmark Index, using an optimisation process. The optimisation process aims
to reduce the carbon intensity and potential emissions, increase the ESG score and minimise the tracking
error, each relative to the Parent Index.



                                                        92

                                                                                            NM0926U-5898621-92/664

=== pdf p.93 ===
The Parent Index is a free float-adjusted market capitalisation weighted index that comprises companies
included in the MSCI World Index that are within the Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS)
communication services sector based on the MSCI's Global Investable Market Indices methodology. The MSCI
World Index measures the performance of large and mid capitalisation stocks across developed market
countries which comply with MSCI's size, liquidity and free-float criteria.

The GICS communication services sector currently comprises companies involved in: (i) telecommunication
services, which includes companies that are involved in fixed-line, cellular, wireless telecommunication
services and internet services providers; and (ii) media and entertainment services, which includes companies
that are involved in advertising, broadcasting, cable and satellite, publishing, movies and entertainment
(including online entertainment streaming companies), interactive home entertainment (i ncluding producers
of mobile gaming applications) and interactive media and services (including search engines, social media
and networking platforms, online classifieds, online review companies and companies involved in content and
information creation or distribution through proprietary platforms). The Parent Index may not include every
category comprising the GICS communication services sector as defined here, or every developed market
country within the MSCI World Index.

The Benchmark Index excludes issuers that are involved in the following business lines/activities (or related
activities): controversial weapons, nuclear weapons, civilian firearms, tobacco, thermal coal, oil sands,
conventional weapons and companies that are classified as violating United Nations Global Compact principles
(which are widely accepted corporate sustainability principles that meet fundamental responsibilities in areas
such as anti-corruption, human rights, labour and the environment). The index provider defines what
constitutes “involvement” in each restricted activity. This may be based on percentage of revenue, a defined
total revenue threshold, or any connection to a restricted activity regardless of the amount of revenue
received.

The Benchmark Index also excludes issuers with a ‘red‘ MSCI ESG Controversy Score which is based on ESG
principles and indicates an issuer's involvement in very severe ESG business controversies that have a negative
ESG impact on its operations, products or services. An MSCI ESG rating is designed to measure an issuer’s
resilience to long-term, industry material ESG risks and how well it manages ESG risks and opportunities relative
to industry peers. The MSCI ESG rating methodology seeks to identify issuers with higher MSCI ESG ratings as
issuers that may be better positioned to manage future ESG-related challenges and that may experience fewer
ESG-related controversies compared to their industry peers. Further details are available on the index provider’s
website at https://www.msci.com/esg-ratings. Issuers that have not been assessed or rated by the index provider
for an ESG Controversy Score, an MSCI ESG rating or ESG Score are excluded from the Benchmark Index.

Following the application of the above exclusionary criteria, the constituents of the Benchmark Index are
selected using the index provider's optimisation methodology which seeks to minimise the ex -ante tracking
error relative to the Parent Index, subject to certain constraints relative to the Parent Index (namely, a
reduction in the weighted average carbon emission intensity, an increase in the weighted average industry -
adjusted ESG score, maximum and minimum constituent weights, country weights) and other constraints (for
example, maximum issuer weight and maximum turnover at each rebalancing).

The Benchmark Index rebalances on a quarterly basis. The Benchmark Index also caps the weight of the
largest companies at each rebalance to help ensure index diversification. The weight of the largest group
entity in the Benchmark Index is capped at 35% and the weights of the remaining group entities are capped
at 20% with a buffer of 10% applied on these limits at each rebalancing. In addition, companies which have
been identified as having a ‘red’ MSCI controversy flag, or which have been classified as vi olating United
Nations Global Compact principles, may also be removed from the Benchmark Index in between index
rebalances in accordance with the index methodology. Further details regarding the Benchmark Index
(including     its  constituents)    are    available    on    the    index     provider’s    website    at
https://www.msci.com/indexes/ishares and https://www.msci.com/constituents.

been identified as having a ‘red’ MSCI controversy flag, or which have been classified as vi olating United
Nations Global Compact principles, may also be removed from the Benchmark Index in between index

iShares MSCI World Energy Sector UCITS ETF

Investment Objective
The investment objective of the Fund is to seek to provide investors with a total return, taking into account both
capital and income returns, which reflects the return of the MSCI World Energy Index.

Investment Policy
In order to achieve this investment objective, the investment policy of the Fund is to invest in a portfolio of equity
securities that, as far as possible and practicable, consists of the component securities of the MSCI World Energy
Index, this Fund’s Benchmark Index. The Fund intends to replicate the constituents of the Benchmark Index by
holding all the securities comprising the Benchmark Index in a similar proportion to their weightings in the
Benchmark Index. In order to replicate its Benchmark Index, this Fund may invest up to 20% of its Net
Asset Value in shares issued by the same body. This limit may be raised to 35% for a single issuer
when exceptional market conditions apply (as set out in section 4 of Schedule III).

The Base Currency of iShares MSCI World Energy Sector UCITS ETF is US Dollar (US$).

Benchmark Index
The MSCI World Energy Index is a free float-adjusted market capitalisation weighted index that comprises
companies included in the MSCI World Index (the "Parent Index") that are within the Global Industry
Classification Standard (GICS) energy sector based on the MSCI's Global Investable Market Indices methodology.

The Parent Index measures the performance of large and mid capitalisation stocks across developed market
countries which comply with MSCI's size, liquidity, and free-float criteria.

The GICS energy sector comprises companies which businesses are dominated by any of the following activities:
The construction or provision of oil rigs, drilling equipment and other energy related service and equipment,
companies engaged in the exploration, production, marketing, refining, storage and/or transportation of oil and
gas products. It also includes companies primarily involved in the production and mining of coal, related products
and other consumable fuels related to the generation of energy.

The Benchmark Index may not include every category comprising the GICS energy sector as defined here, or
every developed market country within the Parent Index. The Benchmark Index rebalances on a quarterly basis.
